steps.title: Doing Great: Celebrate the Win
steps.content:
That’s wonderful to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That’s exactly what we like to hear. That’s the beauty of the wave therapy. It doesn’t mask anything, it actually helps the tissue heal, so when it’s better, it tends to stay better.

Do you remember how bad it was before we treated it? How long you’d been putting up with it before you finally came in?

(Let them answer. Let them relive the win before you move on.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, thank you so much for that information. While I have you on the phone, I’d like to go ahead and finish updating your file by asking you a few quick questions. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes. Almost everyone says yes. You asked permission, and it’s their file.)

steps.title: The Transition: Acknowledge and Ask Permission
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, obviously I know you said {{complaint_reference}} has been coming back, and we’re absolutely going to talk about that. But while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few additional questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Eight Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Critical: write down every area they mention as you go. You’ll recap them in a moment.)

First, other than the area we treated, do you have any OTHER nagging pain that’s been hanging around? A shoulder, an elbow, a knee, a hip? The kind of ache that’s been there so long it feels like part of the furniture.

How about your feet? Any heel or arch pain, especially those first few steps in the morning when you get out of bed? That classic plantar fasciitis pattern responds beautifully to what we do.

Any tendon trouble? Tennis elbow, golfer’s elbow, that spot on the shoulder that lights up when you reach into the back seat or hook a bra strap?

What about old injuries that never fully healed? The ankle you rolled years ago, the pulled muscle that still tightens up, the hip that aches after you’ve been sitting a while or makes you swing your leg out of the car, the knee that’s never been the same since?

Any deep muscle tightness or knots that massage helps for a day and then it’s right back? Those stubborn trigger points in the neck, shoulders, or hips?

Are you currently experiencing any tension, pain, or soreness in the neck, mid-back, or lower back, even if it’s mild, lasts less than five minutes, and goes away on its own?

Is there anything you’ve cut back on? Running, pickleball, the gym, long walks, because something starts barking when you push it?

And finally, what are you doing for these things right now? The Advil, the ice, the braces and sleeves in the drawer? I want the whole picture for your file.

(If they mentioned anything at all, use the notes you took during the questions and ask:)

Now {{contact_first_name}}, you just told me about (read back the issues they mentioned, e.g. “your sleep’s been rough and your back’s been bothering you”). If you could completely eliminate just one of those problems and never have it bother you again, which one would you choose?

(If they genuinely mentioned nothing, skip this question and use the “genuinely nothing” path below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, what I’d like to do now is ask you a few quick questions about {{main_concern}}, so I can get your file fully updated. It’ll only take a minute.

(Take the concern they named and make it real with three questions, in order. Write down or make note of their answers. You will use them in the next section. After each question, pause and let them fully answer. React like a human: “I see,” “Wow,” “That’s a lot.”)

How long have you been experiencing it? A few days, a few weeks, or longer than that? Just a day or two, a few weeks, a month or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer, then:) “[Repeat their answer back]? Would you agree with me that dealing with something like that for that long really isn’t OK?”

(If they shrug it off, “oh, I just deal with it”:) “You know, even a bottle of Tylenol says if it lasts more than a week or so, you should have it looked at. You’ve been dealing with this a lot longer than that.”

Is that something that you notice only once or twice a month, or is it happening more often than that?

(Let them answer, then:)

“And when you are experiencing it, does it seem to be more like first thing in the morning, the middle of the day, while you’re at work, by the end of the day? Or do you feel it multiple times a day, or is it there all day?”

(Let them answer, then:) “That’s a lot. And honestly, having it that often isn’t just not OK. It’s not normal. Wouldn’t you agree?”

And the last thing I’d like to ask is how it’s impacting you. But first, do me a favor: think of a day when you felt great, {{main_concern}} wasn’t in the picture, you were full of energy, everything was clicking. Now think of the absolute worst day you’ve had with it. Do you have those two days in your head?

(Wait for the yes. Then walk the worst day through three areas, pausing after each:)

“On that worst day, what about work? Could you go? And if you did, were you as productive as usual? Were you as enjoyable to be around?” (Let them respond. “I see.”)

“What about at home? Were you fully engaged with the people around you, or did you kind of want to be left alone?” (Let them respond. “That’s really not OK.”)

“And the things you enjoy. Your hobbies, getting together with friends, family things. What happens to those when it’s at its worst?” (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that with me. It makes complete sense, and that’s exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}} help people with every single day.

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds to me like {{main_concern}} isn’t just affecting you. It may also be affecting the people you care about, keeping you from the things you enjoy doing, maybe even getting in the way at work. Do you see how that could actually be the case?

(Wait for their answer. If they say no or hesitate: “That’s completely fair, and honestly, I’m glad it hasn’t spilled over into the rest of your life. But it’s still been bothering you, and that’s reason enough.” Then continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you set up with an appointment so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look at you and see if there’s something {{rec_pronoun}} can do to help you with {{main_concern}}. If {{rec_pronoun}} can help you, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know, and {{rec_pronoun}}’d be honored if you let {{rec_obj}}. And if {{rec_pronoun}} don’t think {{rec_pronoun}} can help, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know that as well, because {{rec_pronoun}}’re not here to waste anybody’s time or money. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you did tell me {{main_concern}} has been showing up and getting to you.

So help me understand. Why wouldn't you want to have it evaluated? What's keeping you from getting it looked at?

(Say this with genuine, confused curiosity, never pushy, and never arguing. You honestly can't see why they wouldn't want something looked at that they just told you is a problem, based on how bad they described it. Then stop talking and let them give you the real reason.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: Nothing Found: The Commitment Question
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I am so glad you’re doing so well, and we’re thrilled to hear it.

Let me ask you this. I remember when you first came in, you told us you were done living around that pain. You wanted it actually fixed, not just quieted down. And you told us that once you got that improvement, you wanted to hold onto it and maintain it. Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Don’t argue with whatever they say. Acknowledge it warmly.)

(Then tap the button below that’s closest to the reason they shared. It will give you a natural, conversational way to respond before inviting them back onto the schedule.)

steps.title: If They Say: "I Was Feeling Fine"
steps.content:
That makes total sense, {{contact_first_name}}, and honestly, that’s the best reason there is. When you feel good, coming in stops feeling urgent. Here’s the funny thing about it, though. Feeling that good is actually the result of the care you did. That tissue is holding strong because of the care you did. The quick checks are what keep it that way.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer. Wait for them to respond before moving on.)

Was there anything else that was holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(Let them answer. If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we go ahead and get you back on the schedule so you can keep feeling as good as you do right now. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I completely understand. That’s real, and I’m glad you told me. What a lot of our practice members have found is that check-in visits are spaced out and cost a fraction of what it takes to fix a problem that’s been sliding for months. And you’re not committing to anything. It’s simply a visit so {{rec_pronoun}} can make sure that tissue is continuing to hold strong.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer. Wait for them to respond before moving on.)

(Do NOT improvise pricing, packages, or discounts on the call. Let the office handle specifics.)

Was there anything else that was holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(Let them answer. If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we go ahead and get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: "Life Got Busy"
steps.content:
Oh, I completely hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and this is exactly the kind of thing that quietly slips off the calendar. No guilt at all; it happens to everyone. The nice part is that a check-in visit is quick, and we can find a time that actually works around your schedule instead of adding to it.

Does that make sense?

Was there anything else that was holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

My recommendation is that we go ahead and get you back on the schedule at a time that’s easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: "I'll Come Back If It Comes Back"
steps.content:
That’s a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}, and I get it. The only thing I’d gently share is that pain is usually the last thing to show up, by the time it hurts, the tissue has often been slipping for a while underneath. Catching it early usually means a quick tweak and you’re back on track, instead of the treatment, time, and money it takes when something has been slipping for months.

Does that make sense?

steps.title: Objection: I thought I was fixed for good
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that's a great thing to bring up. These things can flare back up over time with everyday wear and tear, and that's exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}}'ll want to look at with you in person.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: It came back after I stopped
steps.content:
I completely understand. These things can be stubborn, and once you're out of the rhythm of your sessions they can sometimes try to work their way back. That's exactly why coming in makes sense, so {{rec_pronoun}} can look at the whole picture and talk through the best plan to get you back on track and help you hold your progress.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.content:
I understand, and that can get you by, but I know how much better you felt when you weren't having to just push through it. Coming in is the best way to get {{rec_poss}} eyes on it and get you back to real relief.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I'm considering injections or surgery
steps.content:
I could certainly see where you might be considering that, but many people do like to see where a conservative option fits before making a bigger decision, which is exactly what the appointment is for.

Let me ask you this: if there was a way that we could get you back to feeling good, and that could come with a strategy to keep the symptoms gone and keep you feeling better instead of having to do injections or surgery, is that something you would be interested in?

(Wait for the yes, then go straight back to scheduling.)

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's worth coming in, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Honestly, coming in is really just information. {{rec_pronoun_cap}} takes a look, you find out exactly what's going on with {{main_concern}}, and then you get to decide with real answers instead of wondering. And if we can't help you, we'll tell you that too.

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer or a link can only tell you so much. It can't actually look at what's going on with {{main_concern}} for you specifically. That's really what the visit is for: {{rec_pronoun}} takes a look and you get answers that apply to you, not just general information.
